imperial.name: Cauliflower

actions.text:
Sow

Summer heads Jan under glass or early Apr outside. Autumn heads mid-Apr–mid-May. Winter heads May.

Transplant

Early under glass late Mar–early Apr. Summer Jun, autumn late Jun, winter late Jul.

methods.text:
Sow 

Use a nursery row, tray or modules. Space seeds thinly. Keep growth steady. Discard seedlings that have lost their growing point.

Transplant 

Water nursery rows the day before lifting. Take young sturdy plants with soil around the roots. Set the lowest leaves at soil level, firm well and water. Allow extra space for winter heads.

text:
Cauliflower.
DIFFICULTY
Tricky
4/5
HARVEST SEASONS
Spring / Summer / Autumn / Winter

A cauliflower needs steady growth to make a tight curd. Drought, crowding or a check at transplanting can leave tiny heads. Choose the variety for your season and give it firm soil, water and room.

Quick facts
Harvest

Jan – Apr; Jul – Oct

Germination

7–12 days

Sowing depth

5/8 in.

Yield per plant

1-2 lb

Ready in

From sowing: summer/autumn 18–24 weeks; winter 40–50 weeks

Sow

Summer heads Jan under glass or early Apr outside. Autumn heads mid-Apr–mid-May. Winter heads May.

Row spacing

Summer/autumn 24 in., winter/spring 28 in., minis 6 in..

Plant spacing

Summer/autumn 18–24 in., winter/spring 28 in., minis 6 in..

Transplant

Early under glass late Mar–early Apr. Summer Jun, autumn late Jun, winter late Jul.

Recommended varieties
SUMMER
Clapton F1

A clubroot-resistant white cauliflower; combine with good rotation and soil care.

SUMMER
All The Year Round

White heads for successive sowings; not an all-year outdoor crop.

SUMMER
Graffiti

Purple heads add colour alongside white varieties.

ROMANESCO
Veronica F1

Pointed lime-green Romanesco curds offer distinctive shape and texture.

WINTER
Aalsmeer

An overwintering type for spring crops. Sow in early summer; protect through winter.

Key risks
Club root (finger and toe)

Club root causes swollen, distorted roots, poor growth and wilting in warm weather.

Cabbage caterpillars

Caterpillars chew leaves and can hide in cauliflower curds.

Cabbage root fly

Cabbage root fly maggots tunnel into roots and stems.

Button cauliflowers

Tiny premature heads can follow growth checks from drought, poor fertility, crowded or root-bound plants, transplant stress or pest damage.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
38
BRASSICAS

Prepare well ahead.

Add compost in autumn and let the bed settle.

Keep growth steady.

Water reliably, especially while curds form.

Soil & preparation
Use sunny, rich, moist, well-drained soil with room for large types. Add autumn compost or rotted manure; let the bed settle.
Avoid poor soil. Feed organically if needed. Rake and firm before planting, without forking.
Sowing & planting
Raise seedlings
Firm into the bed
Sow 

Use a nursery row, tray or modules. Space seeds thinly. Keep growth steady. Discard seedlings that have lost their growing point.

Transplant 

Water nursery rows the day before lifting. Take young sturdy plants with soil around the roots. Set the lowest leaves at soil level, firm well and water. Allow extra space for winter heads.

Looking after the crop
Hoe carefully; protect against birds and caterpillars with fine mesh held clear of leaves.
Water reliably during establishment and curd formation. Mulch with compost; feed weak plants organically without disturbing roots.
Cover white curds with outer leaves against sun, and winter curds against frost and snow. Purple types need no blanching.
Harvesting & storage
Check inside the central leaves. A small curd can swell rapidly in a week or two.
Cut each curd while tight. A rough surface or separating florets mean the head is starting to flower.
Cut below the head. Each plant gives one curd, then the ground can be cleared.
Pests & diseases
Problem	What to look for	What to do
Club root (finger and toe)	Swollen roots; wilting.	Avoid infected soil; clean tools. Test before liming; no cure.
Cabbage caterpillars	Holes; feeding caterpillars.	Hand-pick eggs and larvae; use fine mesh.
Cabbage root fly	Wilting; tunnelled roots.	Use collars or mesh on a rotated bed.
Button cauliflowers	Tiny premature heads.	Prevent drought, crowding and other growth checks.
Blind plants	No central growing bud.	Discard blind seedlings before planting.
Slugs and snails	Holes; seedlings eaten.	Hand-pick at dusk; clear yellow leaves near seedlings.
Mealy aphid	Grey colonies; curled leaves.	Squash damaging colonies; encourage predators.
Flea beetle	Tiny holes; jumping beetles.	Mesh young plants; keep growth steady.
Boron deficiency	Hollow stems; brown curds.	Test soil. Avoid excess lime and correct a confirmed shortage.
Whiptail	Narrow, strap-like leaves.	Test soil; correct acidity and confirmed deficiency.
Final tips

After peas or beans, keep soil settled; avoid pulling roots out.

Mini varieties need closer spacing than maincrops.

Cut heads when ready, even if still small.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
See also: Vegetable Troubles 106–111 · Growing Techniques 150
39
BRASSICAS
